The genus Orthoebolavirus, known as Ebolavirus (- or ; ee-BOH-lə- or ə-BOH-lə-VY-rəs) until 2023, is a virological taxon included in the family Filoviridae (filament-shaped viruses), order Mononegavirales. The members of this genus are called ebolaviruses, and encode their genome in the form of single-stranded negative-sense RNA. The six known virus species are named for the region where each was originally identified: Bundibugyo ebolavirus, Reston ebolavirus, Sudan ebolavirus, Taï Forest ebolavirus (originally Côte d'Ivoire ebolavirus), Zaire ebolavirus (also known as Ebola virus), and Bombal
